vignette:
Omar sits across from me, a man of 54 years, with deep-set eyes that seem to carry the weight of countless stories. He is a community organizer, a role he has embraced for over two decades, dedicating himself to uplifting marginalized voices in his neighborhood. Yet today, there is a heaviness in his demeanor, a somberness that belies the passion he once exuded. As he begins to recount his experiences, I can see the flickers of anger, shame, and despair that ripple beneath his calm surface.

His narrative begins several years ago, when he had just married Lena, a woman he thought would be a partner in every sense. Their early days were filled with laughter, shared dreams, and plans for a future. But as the months passed, the idyllic image began to crack. Omar recalls the first instance of violence—a moment that he still struggles to comprehend. "It was a simple argument about money," he says, his voice wavering slightly. "I didn’t think it would escalate." He remembers feeling trapped as Lena’s frustration morphed into rage, her voice rising in a way he had never witnessed before. It started with a shove, then a slap, and in an instant, the woman he loved transformed into someone unrecognizable.

As he shares this, his hands clench into fists, a physical manifestation of the memories that continue to haunt him. He describes how, in the aftermath, he felt a strange mix of anger and bewilderment. He thought about leaving, but the fear of what Lena might do—both to him and to herself—held him in place. “It’s like being in a storm and not knowing which way to turn,” he says, his brow furrowing in thought. 

Omar tries to compartmentalize his life, throwing himself into his work as a community organizer. He becomes a champion for others, advocating for justice and support for those who suffer. But inside, he is unraveling. The unpredictability of Lena’s moods forces him into a state of hypervigilance. At community meetings, he feels a gnawing anxiety that he cannot shake. The sounds of laughter and discussion around him feel foreign, almost suffocating. He finds himself scanning the room, looking for exits, ready to bolt at the first sign of trouble.

The physical abuse becomes a cycle, an inescapable loop of violence followed by remorse. Lena apologizes, cries, and promises change, and for a while, Omar clings to the hope that things will improve. But the cycle repeats. Each time, it shreds his sense of self a little more. He begins to withdraw from friends and colleagues, fearing that they will judge him, or worse, that they will blame him for provoking Lena. “They wouldn’t understand,” he mutters, shaking his head as if to dismiss any notion of seeking help. 

His nights are plagued by nightmares—vivid reenactments of the abuse, where he feels the sting of the slap again, the weight of fear pressing down on him. He wakes up in a cold sweat, gasping for breath, the shadows in the room morphing into the familiar silhouette of Lena. It is a torment that lingers throughout his day, casting a pall over even the simplest tasks. 

In the present, he describes the toll this has taken on his marriage. Though he still loves Lena, the fear has built an insurmountable wall between them. “I can’t trust her,” he admits, his voice cracking. “I don’t know if she will turn again, and it makes me feel so weak.” He feels as though he is constantly on guard, unable to relax even in moments of peace. 

Omar’s work, once a source of pride and fulfillment, has become a battleground of its own. He finds it increasingly difficult to connect with the community he serves, often feeling overwhelmed by the struggles of others. The weight of their stories, coupled with his own, creates a suffocating pressure that leaves him exhausted.

As he shares these experiences, I notice the flicker of determination in his eyes, a desire to reclaim his narrative. He speaks of wanting to break the cycle—not just for himself, but for others who might be trapped in similar situations. But the journey feels daunting. With each session, he grapples with the ghosts of his past, slowly learning to navigate the path toward healing, even as the shadows loom large.
